boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 40:1 opens with the dateline בְּאַרְבַּ֤ע עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה אַחַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֻכְּתָ֖ה הָעִ֑יר ('after the city was struck') -- the fourteenth and last of the book's fourteen year-bearing datelines -- paired in the same verse with the hand-of-YHWH idiom הָיְתָ֤ה עָלַי֙ יַד יְהוָ֔ה and the transport verb וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתִ֖י שָֽׁמָּה (oshb:Ezek.40.1). This dateline-hand-transport cluster is the strongest onset class the book offers and is also a HARD seam: no row may cross it. It follows immediately, without intervening material, the utterance formula and pe (oshb:Ezek.39.29, single-witness) that close the preceding unit. The frame continues at 40:2 with the header בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֔ים 'in the visions of God' (one of only three such headers in the book) plus a further transport pair (הֱבִיאַ֖נִי / וַיְנִיחֵ֗נִי (oshb:Ezek.40.2)), and again at 40:3 (וַיָּבֵ֨יא אוֹתִ֜י שָׁ֗מָּה (oshb:Ezek.40.3)) introducing the measuring man. Close side: 40:4 carries no formula-grade close device; the seam at 40:4/40:5 rests on the man's charge, הַגֵּ֛ד אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.40.4) 'declare all that you see to the house of Israel', read as ending the entry scene before the measuring reed is put to use in 40:5's וַיָּ֜מָד (oshb:Ezek.40.5), the first of an eighteen-verse run of that verb across 40:5-41:5. Both sides are weighed: the onset is the best-evidenced in the whole span; the close is a content judgment (charge-speech versus measuring-action), not a refrain, and is held accordingly.

K/Q at 41:15 is a lexical/form variant on 'galleries', not a numeral; no other K/Q or editorial note touches this row. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: five occurrences over four verses (41:12, two on 41:16, 41:17, 41:19); no intra-verse position is sourceable from the extract.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:1 opens with a double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי אֶל הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה ... וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי אֶל הַלִּשְׁכָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.42.1) 'he brought me out into the outer court ... then he brought me into the room' -- the strongest onset in the span after 40:1 and 43:1 -- moving the tour to the priests' chambers, first north-side (42:1-9) then, by parallel description, south-side (42:10-12). Close side: 42:13-14 supplies the row's function, delivered as a genuine speak-formula, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.42.13) 'he said to me': these are the holy chambers where the priests eat the most holy things and must change garments before approaching the people -- a law-toned close inside a measurement row, disclosed rather than reclassified. Both the double transport at onset and the speak-formula at close are tier-1 devices, making this one of the better-evidenced rows here despite the total absence of parashah corroboration in these chapters.

oshb:Ezek.42.9 (K/Q, doubled note, checked: word-division/spelling variants on 'from under these chambers' and 'the entrance', not a numeral)

strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the north-side (42:1-9) and south-side (42:10-12) chamber descriptions into two rows was weighed and rejected: 42:10-12 explicitly cross-references the north-side description ('like the appearance of the rooms which were toward the north') rather than opening an independent unit, and carries no transport verb of its own.

device_notes: No parashah mark in ch 42. Two K/Q verses disclosed (42:9 doubled, 42:14 single), both checked: neither touches a numeral. Content disclosure, not a category deviation: 42:13-14 states a food-purity law for the chambers just measured; the row is classed temple_measurement because the chamber dimensions (42:1-12) dominate it and the law clause closes rather than opens the unit. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: three occurrences over two verses (42:10, and two on 42:13); no intra-verse position is sourceable from the extract.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:15 opens with the completion notice וְכִלָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.42.15) 'when he had finished' ... 'measuring the inner house', paired with the transport verb וְהוֹצִיאַ֨נִי֙ 'he brought me out' -- a close-grade formula pressed into onset service here, since it explicitly marks the end of the inner-house survey that has run since 40:5 before turning outward to the perimeter wall. Four cardinal-direction measurements follow (east 42:16, north 42:17, south 42:18, west 42:19), each opening with a measure verb on its own line, then a summary at 42:20. Close side: 42:20 ends on the wall's purpose, לְהַבְדִּ֕יל בֵּ֥ין הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ לְחֹֽל (oshb:Ezek.42.20) 'to make a separation between the holy and the common' -- a genuine thematic close, and the point at which the whole measuring circuit that opened at 40:5 ends, immediately before 43:1's transport verb and the glory's return open a new kind of scene. Both sides of this seam are unusually well aligned: a completion-formula onset and a purpose-clause close on one side, a transport-plus-glory onset on the other.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Ezek.42.15 (completion formula + transport verb, closing the measuring circuit opened at 40:5)
oshb:Ezek.42.16 (measure verb; K/Q, single note, a lexical spelling variant flagged in the disclosure inventory but not affecting the reed-count itself)

One K/Q verse disclosed (42:16), a lexical spelling variant, not a numeral. boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:1's transport verb opens וַיּוֹלִכֵ֖נִי אֶל הַשָּׁ֑עַר (oshb:Ezek.43.1) 'he led me to the gate', beginning the named hard seam behind the closed measuring circuit, and the row immediately carries the glory-of-YHWH device twice (43:4, 43:5), part of the book's nine-verse departure/return arc for that idiom, alongside the river-Chebar inclusio at 43:3 (one of eight such verses tying this scene back to Ezek 1 and 10) and 'I fell on my face' (one of five). The row turns from vision report to direct address at 43:6-9: a voice from the house, the man beside the prophet, the 'son of man' charge naming YHWH's throne and footstool, and the polemic against the house of Israel's defilement of the sanctuary by royal corpses and high places. Close side: 43:9 ends the divine resolution וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם (oshb:Ezek.43.9) 'then I will dwell among them forever' immediately before the samekh (oshb:Ezek.43.9, single-witness) -- the first Masoretic paragraph mark since the pe at oshb:Ezek.39.29, ending a 103-verse unmarked stretch. This is the only row here whose close carries genuine parashah corroboration, and it is disclosed as single-witness even so.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:10 opens אַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם (oshb:Ezek.43.10) 'you, son of man' directly after the samekh (single-witness) closing at oshb:Ezek.43.9 -- a near-form of the book's twenty-three-verse 'and you, son of man' sub-onset family, here without the leading vav, disclosed as such rather than counted against that sweep. It charges the prophet to show the house's pattern so Israel may be ashamed of its iniquities. Close side: 43:12 closes on a doubled envelope formula, זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֣ת הַבָּ֑יִת ... הִנֵּה זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֥ת הַבָּֽיִת (oshb:Ezek.43.12) 'this is the law of the house ... behold, this is the law of the house', repeating the title at the top and bottom of the same verse -- a strong lexical close-device, and the reason this three-verse span is held as its own row despite its length: the inclusio is a self-contained frame around 43:10-12 that a larger row would have to break through rather than around.

One K/Q verse disclosed (43:11, doubled note), checked: both disputed forms are possessive-suffix/grammatical-number variants on 'form' and 'law', not numerals. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: one occurrence, at 43:12, the same verse as the doubled inclusio close. Over-split guard: held at 3 verses on the strength of the disclosed sub-onset at 43:10 and the doubled inclusio close at 43:12, not a word-event unit.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:13 opens with an explicit topic header, וְאֵ֨לֶּה מִדּ֤וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ (oshb:Ezek.43.13) 'and these are the measurements of the altar', functioning as a list-onset in the same way such headers do elsewhere in the book, immediately after the doubled inclusio that closes 43:12. The row descends through the altar's base, lower and greater ledges, hearth and horns, in cubit-and-handbreadth units, one of which (43:15) carries both an OSHB anomalous-form note and a K/Q note on the same word, disclosed together. Close side: 43:17 ends with the steps 'toward the east' before 43:18 opens with the messenger formula, a clean tier-1 onset on the far side even though this row's own close rests on content completion rather than a refrain.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:18 opens with בֶּן אָדָם֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.43.18) 'son of man, thus says the Lord YHWH' -- one of the book's 122 messenger-formula verses, and the clearest speech-onset here after the throne declaration of 43:1-9 -- introducing the altar's dedication ordinances. The utterance formula נְאֻ֛ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה (oshb:Ezek.43.19) appears mid-unit at 43:19, read as paragraph-final rather than row-final since the seven-day consecration instructions continue without interruption. The row carries the young-bull sin offering, the blood rite on the horns and corners, the second-day goat, the seven-day consecration, and closes at 43:27 on the same utterance formula, וְרָצִ֣אתִי אֶתְכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.43.27) 'then I will accept you, says the Lord YHWH', this time genuinely row-final. Close side: immediately after that utterance the verse carries two consecutive samekh marks, the sole doubled occurrence among the book's marked verses (sweep: 183 verses) -- making 43:27 the best-attested close available and, since it is also this assignment's own boundary, the strongest evidence for ending it exactly here. Both sides converge unusually cleanly here: a messenger-formula onset opposite an utterance-plus-doubled-mark close.
